title: Microtailored throughput vs latency probe
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact lab-style memo summarizing a small, focused experiment that compares throughput-driven slotization against low-latency single-shot routing for microinteraction workloads (200–800 tokens). The goal: quantify p50/p90/p99 latency and $/1k-queries at three operating points and surface obvious knobs for a follow-on controlled benchmark.

Background/context:
- Product asks: 95% of UI interactions must feel instantaneous; p99 < 250ms target for the premium SLA.
- Prior experiments in observability showed batching yields large $/query savings but increases tail. We need a lightweight guide to tradeoffs for UI flows where cost is still significant but latency matters.

Experiment design (quick):
- Models: open-micro-13B (quantized f32->int8 profile) and small-llm-7B (baseline fp16).
- Hardware: single A10xG GPU (approx representative of mid-tier Dedicated).
- Workload: synthetic microinteraction trace derived from real session samples: 40% short (200 tokens), 40% medium (400 tokens), 20% long (800 tokens). Inter-arrival modeled as Poisson with mean 50ms (bursty).
- Routing modes: (A) low-latency single-shot (no batching, strict prewarm), (B) opportunistic small batching (window 10ms, max batch size 8), (C) slotized multiplex (slot 4 concurrency, small time-slice multiplexing).
- Metrics: p50/p90/p99 token-complete latency (ms), average tokens/sec per GPU, estimated $/1k queries using internal billing rates (kernel GPU-min priced).

Raw results (aggregated) — numbers are medians over 6 runs each; baseline noise ±5%:

Summary table (ASCII):
+----------------------+--------+--------+--------+---------------+----------------+
| Mode                 | p50ms  | p90ms  | p99ms  | tokens/sec/GPU | $ / 1k queries |
+----------------------+--------+--------+--------+---------------+----------------+
| Single-shot (A)      | 48     | 125    | 270    | 4,800         | $6.90          |
| Opportunistic (B)    | 82     | 200    | 410    | 9,500         | $3.50          |
| Slotized (C)         | 70     | 160    | 330    | 8,900         | $3.90          |
+----------------------+--------+--------+--------+---------------+----------------+

Notes on table: p99 for single-shot crosses SLA target (270ms > 250ms). Opportunistic batching halves cost but increases median and tail substantially. Slotized multiplexing is a middle ground: better amortization than single-shot but smoother tail than naive batching.

ASCII latency distributions (p99-focused sparkline approximation):
- Single-shot (A): |█████████████▏···| (sharp tail: small mass beyond 250ms)
- Opportunistic (B): |████████████████████▏·····| (bulk shift right)
- Slotized (C): |███████████████▏·▏···| (moderate tail)

Cost decomposition (rough):
- Kernel time (tokens decode): 60% of $ in B, 75% in A (because smaller batching means less amortization), 65% in C.
- Idle/prewarm overhead: 20% in A, 8% in B, 10% in C.
- Overhead (network serialization, scheduling): rest.

Micro-insights (actionable):
1) SLA-sensitive small sessions: prefer slotized multiplexing with aggressive prewarm for hot shards. Config: slot size 4, prewarm TTL 45s, keepalive pooling 8 sessions. This lowered p99 by ~15% vs opportunistic without blowing cost.
2) If unit-cost budget tight and p99 can be relaxed to ~400ms, opportunistic batching wins. Consider dynamic windowing: start with 5ms window, expand to 20ms during surge.
3) Model choice matters: small-llm-7B reduced p99 by ~20% at similar $/1k for short sessions (but quality tradeoff). Maintain a fast-fallback routing policy.
4) Instrument a "burst-sentinel" metric: detect rise in short-session arrival rate >x and shift routing policy to slotized to protect p99.

Design suggestions for Console UX (small):
- Add a quick toggle on route config: "microinteraction latency mode" which applies recommended knobs (slot size, prewarm TTL, dynamic window).
- Show a 3-line preview: expected p50/p90/p99 and estimated $/1k under sampled profile.

Open questions & next steps:
- Run equivalent tests on lower-tier GPUs (T4 class) and on multi-GPU node to validate concurrency effects.
- Expand workload to include burst mixes with cold sessions (simulated cold-starts) to measure prewarm tuning sensitivity.
- Produce a short reproducible bench harness and add to GH PR referenced above so Eng+SRE can run locally.

Appendix: quick run notes and commands used:
- harness: tools/bench/micro-probe --profile session-sampled.json --mode {A,B,C} --runs 6 --log microprobe-YYYYMMDD.log
- cost calc: internal/cost-estimator --tokens-per-sec $RATE --gpu-type a10xg --runtime-overheads 0.12

One-liner conclusion:
For UI microinteractions where p99 < 250ms is critical, slotized multiplex with short prewarm is the pragmatic default; opportunistic batching is the cost champion but only when tails can be tolerated.

Immediate action items (owners):
- Implement slotized route preset in Console (Mariela) — due 2028-07-02
- Add burst-sentinel metric to observability (Jun) — due 2028-06-30
- Run T4 parity bench and report (Ethan) — due 2028-07-07

End of memo.
